goal: Build the incident evidence trail: query Events as API objects with server-side field selectors, drive kubectl logs across containers and restarts, and establish exactly what kubectl top requires on a kind cluster that does not ship metrics-server.
produces: A namespace emitting a real mixed event stream (Normal, Warning FailedMount, Warning BackOff) filtered with compound --field-selector queries
A two-container Pod proving that only stdout/stderr reaches kubectl logs, plus a crash-looping container whose cause is only visible via --previous
A completed event-triage worksheet recording each query, what it returned, and whether kubectl top was available (Path A install or Path B skip)
concepts: Events are aggregated (count + firstTimestamp) and garbage-collected after --event-ttl, one hour by default — a triage signal, never an audit log
Field selectors are server-side but restricted to indexed fields: type, reason and involvedObject.* are selectable, message is not
kubectl logs captures only stdout/stderr, retains one previous container generation, and is bounded by kubelet log rotation — the case for node-level shippers
kubectl top is an add-on requiring metrics-server behind the aggregation layer; on kind it needs --kubelet-insecure-tls, and it holds no history
